Simulate the raw impacts that studies would report

Source: R/simulate.R
simulate_raw_impacts.Rd

For validation: given a population whose disease combinations follow the maximum-entropy distribution of model (see fit_joint()), and known true additive impacts (and optional interactions), computes what a study would estimate for each disease: the crude difference between animals with and without the disease, or the coefficient of an additive regression adjusted for other diseases. With n = NULL the exact population values are returned; with n set, n animals are sampled, which adds sampling error.

Usage

simulate_raw_impacts(
  model,
  true_impacts,
  interactions = NULL,
  estimand = "crude",
  adjusted_for = NA_character_,
  n = NULL,
  joint = NULL,
  units = NULL
)

Arguments

model

A cm_population() or cm_model() (its impacts are ignored).

true_impacts

Named numeric vector of true impacts, one per disease (any units).

interactions

Optional cm_interactions() with true interaction values (same units).

estimand

"crude" or "adjusted_linear", one per disease or recycled.

adjusted_for

For "adjusted_linear": adjustment sets (ids separated by ";", or "all"), one per disease or recycled.

n

Optional number of animals to sample.

joint

Optional pre-computed fit_joint() result.

units

Optional units label for the returned impacts.

Value

A cm_impacts() object with the simulated raw impacts.

Details

Adjusting the returned raw impacts with deconflate() should recover true_impacts exactly (for n = NULL): with the simultaneous or global method without interactions, and with the global method with them.

Examples

raw <- simulate_raw_impacts(example_supplement(), c(d1 = 2, d2 = 4, d3 = 6))
raw$value
#> [1] 2.421306 5.406438 6.668175
deconflate(cm_model(example_supplement(), raw))$adjusted$adjusted
#> [1] 2 4 6
